He, however, managed to return to the game and finish with six points and eight assists. “Medyo kinabahan kami sa nangyari kay Adrian. Again it was Cliff Hodge. Dami ng ganung insidente ni Cliff Hodge. He is the dirtiest player in the league, I think,” said Guiao during the post-game press conference “Dapat siguro tingnan ng liga ‘yan. He is a danger to the other players in the game. His record speaks for itself,” he added. Hodge was assessed with an unsportsman-like foul but still that didn’t prevent Guiao from calling the Meralco forward out. “Sinaksak niya ‘yung paa niya eh. Kaya siya tinawagan ng unsportsmanlike foul. Maraming incidents na ganun na I think cause danger to the players. It’s always been a lot of situations and incidents that Hodge is involved in. Tingin ko it’s a danger to his fellow players,” Guiao furthered. It wasn’t the first time that Hodge got tangled in such controversy. Fans heavily criticized Hodge over an elbow that landed to the face of Kyt Jimenez and resulted in SMB guard’s fracture of the eye socket. Hodge was also once suspended for a dangerous tackle on Zavier Lucero while he was also called for a Flagrant Foul penalty 2 when his knee hit the face of Mark Barroca in a separate incident. While Hodge simply shrugged the comments off, Guiao’s remarks, however, did not sit well for the Bolts franchise who came into the defense of their veteran player. Meralco stressed that it holds its coaches, players, and staff to always observe the highest level of professionalism, decorum, and conduct in all their games. The team explained that the incident with Nocum and Hodge was purely incidental and should not be misconstrued as a dirty play. The team said Guiao’s comments were unfair and uncalled for. “We therefore take very strong exception to the unfair, unfounded, and unprofessional statement that the head coach of Rain or Shine, Coach Yeng Guiao, uttered in public during his post-game interview against our player, Mr. Cliff Hodge, whom he unjustly maligned in public by calling him ‘the dirtiest player in the PBA,” it said in the statement.

Pax Silica could be 'Trojan horse' for dangerous small modular reactors, says Tinio. Is the Pax Silica project just a "Trojan horse" for something potentially dangerous to Filipinos? ACT Teachers Party-list Rep. Antonio Tinio made this insinuation amid reports that the Marcos administration was considering the use of small modular reactors (SMR) to meet the staggering five-gigawatt power requirement of the planned Pax Silica Economic Security Zone in Clark. The Makabayan solon and House deputy minority leader described the SMRs as "untested and dangerous". Tinio is basing his assertion on the recent signing of the United States (US) and Philippines "123 Agreement" on civil nuclear cooperation. And it didn't take long for him come up with a possible doomsday scenario. “We see a dangerous convergence here. First, the government commits to a US-led project that will consume a huge chunk of our national power supply for the benefit of foreign corporations. Then, it uses the resulting artificial energy crisis to justify importing risky, experimental nuclear technology from the same foreign power,” he said. "[SMRs] remain largely unproven at commercial scale and could be far more expensive than promised. They still pose risks involving radioactive waste, accidents, security, and nuclear proliferation—while their smaller size does not eliminate these fundamental dangers," noted the militant lawmaker. Tinio further says Pax Silica "is a problem of its own making" and an "unnecessary project that will hog electricity needed by our people and industries". He added that it cannot now be used as "an excuse to bring in microreactors and other nuclear technologies that turn our communities into testing grounds and radioactive hazards". The solon pointed out that the Philippines already suffers from the most expensive electricity in Southeast Asia due to the privatization and deregulation of the power sector under the Electric Power Industry Reform Act (EPIRA) law. Scrap Pax Silica Diverting five gigawatts to Pax Silica will worsen shortages and spike prices for ordinary Filipinos, he claimed. “The solution is not to compound one disastrous policy with another. The solution is to scrap Pax Silica, which is a brazen resource grab, and to prioritize genuine national development and energy security for the Filipino people,” Tinio stated. He emphasized that the push for modular nuclear power, facilitated by the 123 Agreement, is driven by US corporate and strategic interests, not by the needs of the Philippines. “The Marcos administration is creating a crisis through Pax Silica and then offering a US-made modular nuclear ‘solution’ that will make us permanently dependent on American technology, fuel, and capital. This is not energy independence; this is deepening neocolonial control over our energy sector,” Tinio argued. He called on the public to vigorously oppose both the Pax Silica project and the introduction of modular nuclear power.

Heat, water cuts deepen hardship in quake-hit Kumamoto. MASHIKI, Kumamoto Pref. (Jiji Press) -- Scorching heat waves and widespread water outages are adding to the hardships faced by more than 9,000 evacuees in areas devastated by Tuesday's powerful earthquake in Kumamoto Prefecture, southwestern Japan. With the quake-hit areas marking their first weekend since the disaster, volunteer activities have begun in the town of Mashiki in Kumamoto. The death toll from the quake, which registered a seismic intensity of up to 7, the highest on the Japanese scale, reached 36, including two deaths that may be linked to the disaster, according to the prefecture's disaster response headquarters. The prefecture has confirmed the identities of 27 victims, and plans to release their names after obtaining the consent of the bereaved families. As of 7 p.m. Saturday, 9,045 people were staying at 218 evacuation centers across the prefecture. While power has been largely restored, many residents have continued sleeping in their vehicles to escape the heat and use their cars' air conditioning. The total number of damaged homes stands at 3,649, more than double the figure reported Friday. Of these, 181 were completely destroyed and 225 were partially damaged. The Japan Meteorological Agency forecast daily highs of at least 35 degrees Celsius through Thursday, with temperatures expected to reach 40 degrees or higher on Monday. It warned that dangerous heat would persist and urged residents to take precautions against heatstroke. About 69,400 households remained without water, with no timetable for restoring the water supply. The disaster response headquarters has stepped up emergency water distribution by compiling information from national, prefectural and municipal authorities to prioritize water truck dispatches. A volunteer center opened Saturday in Mashiki, where work began to remove household items damaged by the quake as part of recovery efforts. The towns of Kashima and Mifune also started seeking volunteer workers. At the Aeon Mall Kumamoto shopping facility in Kashima, where an explosion occurred following the earthquake, police, firefighters and Self-Defense Forces personnel completed their search for anyone who might have been trapped by noon Saturday. After cleaning debris, they concluded that no one was left behind at the site. The earthquake struck at about 4:27 p.m. Tuesday with its epicenter in the Kumamoto region, recording an intensity of up to 7 in the city of Uki and the town of Hikawa, and up to upper 6 in the city of Yatsushiro, Kumamoto Prefecture's namesake capital, Kashima and elsewhere.

Kumamoto shop in Tokyo crowded with visitors after quake. TOKYO (Jiji Press) -- Visitors have formed a long line every day to enter a Tokyo shop promoting specialty products of Kumamoto Prefecture to support the southwestern Japan prefecture hit by Tuesday's huge earthquake. They aim to support people in areas devastated by the quake with an estimated magnitude of 7.1 by purchasing such goods and making donations. According to the Kumamoto prefectural government's Tokyo office, sales at the Ginza Kumamotokan shop on Wednesday were more than twice as high as those on a holiday during the peak season. "It's rare to see such a line," an official said. "Ikinari dango," a traditional Kumamoto confectionery featuring sweet potato and sweet bean paste, and "karashi renkon," or lotus roots stuffed with mustard, are selling well, shop officials said. "I can't do anything because I can't send relief supplies for a while," said a self-employed woman, 56, from Urayasu, Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo. She has a relative in the town of Hikawa, Kumamoto, whose house was damaged by the earthquake. "I bought (items) as this is all I can do," she also said. She expressed a desire to buy whistles featuring Kumamon, the official prefectural mascot, to distribute them to her family for use in the event of future disasters to attract the attention of emergency services. A 64-year-old male corporate employee from Tokyo's Itabashi Ward, who visited the city of Kumamoto on a business trip in July, said, "I could have been affected by the disaster myself." He added, "I bought sweets because I wanted to support (affected people) as much as I could." A total of about 2 million yen was raised in a donation box at the shop on Wednesday and Thursday. "The warm feelings (of visitors) have been a support and encouragement for the people of the prefecture," Mitsuo Matsuoka, a senior official of the Tokyo office, said, while asking for continued support and cooperation.

Centeno, Amit stay in world 10-ball hunt. Chezka Centeno and Rubilen Amit posted contrasting results against their American rivals but stayed in the hunt for a spot in the knockout stage of the 2026 WPA Women’s 10-Ball World Championship in Rome, Italy on Sunday, Aug. 2. The defending champion Centeno, who was relegated to the losers’ bracket after bowing to Amit in the second round, blanked Kennedy Meyman, 4-0, 4-0, to remain in contention in the double elimination stage. Last year’s finalist Amit, meanwhile, yielded to Sofia Mast, 3-4, 4-2,4-1, to join Centeno in the losers’ qualification. Centeno needed two more victories to barge into the Last 16 where the recently-crowned world 8-ball champion must hurdle Indonesia’s Silviana Lu first to arrange a meeting with seasoned player Pia Filler to advance. Amit, for her part, only needed to win her match against the winner between France’s Rachelle Enfroy and Argentina’s Soledad Ayala to make it to the next phase. Centeno and Amit both seek historic third world 10-ball titles, with Centeno also hoping to become the first player to win back-to-back trophies. Her first title came in 2023. Amit, meanwhile, won the inaugural staging in 2009 and repeated it in 2013, both held in Manila. Already advancing to the Last 16 are Mast, Japan’s Yuki Hiraguchi and Chihiro Kawahara, American Savannah Easton, China’s Shi Tianqi and Chen Siming, Margarita Fefilova and Chinese Taipei’s Chen Chia Hua.

Inflation, weak state spending seen dragging Q2 growth to post-pandemic low. Elevated inflation, sluggish state spending, and rising import costs may have dragged Philippine gross domestic product (GDP) growth down to 2.5 percent in the second quarter, slowing further from an already five-year low of 2.8 percent in the previous quarter. Frankfurt-based Deutsche Bank AG expects second-quarter GDP growth to decelerate amid overheating price pressures. “Household consumption likely continued to decelerate in the quarter amid the spike in inflation, which averaged 6.8 percent year-on-year in the second quarter, up from 2.8 percent in the first quarter,” Deutsche Bank Research wrote in a July 31 commentary. If realized, Deutsche Bank’s second-quarter forecast would fall short of the government's revised GDP growth target of 3.5 percent to 4.5 percent. Average growth for the first half, which could come in at 2.7 percent, would also miss the mark. In addition, the Marcos administration spent its budget at a slower-than-usual pace during the first half of 2026. Deutsche Bank noted that the state disbursed 46.7 percent of its planned expenditures—below the five-year average of 47.7 percent for the comparable period. “Net trade is likely to exert a heavier drag on headline growth as costlier imports of fuel and raw materials more than offset AI tailwinds for electronics exports,” the German lender added. Meanwhile, think tank Moody’s Analytics projected the Philippine economy to have picked up to 3 percent in the second quarter—though still tracking below the government’s full-year target. “Stronger government spending and modest export growth likely provided support in the June quarter, while elevated inflation and higher borrowing costs likely weighed on household consumption and private investment,” Moody’s said. Reflecting the broader economic deceleration, household spending growth hit a five-year low of three percent in the first quarter. While borrowing costs were already on an upward trajectory early in the year, persistent price pressures forced the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) to tighten monetary policy further to curb demand and cool inflation. Since Middle East hostilities erupted in late February, the BSP has raised key rates twice, bringing the benchmark rate to 4.75 percent. Much of the inflationary shock stemmed from prolonged military hostilities involving the United States and Iran surrounding the Strait of Hormuz, where transit disruptions choked off roughly 20 percent of the world's oil supply. Deutsche Bank noted that moderating energy costs may have offered slight relief, estimating headline inflation at 6.4 percent in July—unchanged from the two-month low seen in June. “We forecast headline inflation to remain unchanged at 6.4 percent year-on-year in July, as the moderation in energy prices could be offset by increases in food prices, particularly rice,” Deutsche Bank said. In June, the BSP raised its average inflation forecasts for 2026 and 2027 to 6.4 percent and 4.5 percent, respectively, from previous estimates of 6.3 percent and 4.3 percent—with both remaining well above its two percent to four percent target tolerance band.

Mayor Isko orders Meralco to fix 12,000 unsafe poles across Manila. Manila Mayor Francisco “Isko Moreno” Domagoso has ordered Meralco to clear and replace more than 12,000 damaged and leaning electric poles across the city, flagged through government mapping that assessed over 33,000 posts. City data showed more than 6,000 poles were damaged while another 6,000 were leaning, prompting Domagoso to push for immediate action with no area prioritized over another. During a consultative meeting on “systems loss” charges, the mayor said all unserviceable poles identified through the city’s ArcGIS mapping must be addressed. Meralco, in response, committed to speed up the clearing of idle posts and submit a timeline for completion. “There may be some shortcomings in the past, but we try to correct it today and in the future. You have a friend in the City,” Domagoso said. The mayor also assured protection for Meralco crews conducting anti-pilferage operations, tapping the Manila Police District . “Itong mga ito ay nagtatrabaho lang (These people are just doing their jobs), they should not be put in harm’s way,” he said. Meralco officials, meanwhile, revealed that some barangay officials allegedly maintain illegal power connections and have obstructed enforcement operations. The city government said it will coordinate with concerned barangays to resolve access and right-of-way issues, and ordered the creation of a real-time coordination channel among the city, police, and Meralco to speed up field operations.

MPBL pursues deeper probe Into Bacolod franchise. The removal of the Bacolod Masskara franchise from the remainder of the SportsPlus MPBL 2026 Season, together with the lifetime suspension imposed on the players and coaches covered by the league's disciplinary action, underscores Commissioner Emmer Oreta's unwavering commitment to protecting the integrity of the Maharlika Pilipinas Basketball League (MPBL). "When I assumed the role of Commissioner for MPBL Season 8, I made one commitment clear: to strengthen the integrity of the league through decisive and consistent action. Every action we have taken since then reflects that commitment," Oreta said. Since the start of the season, the league has consistently enforced its integrity measures. In April 2026, the MPBL issued a Yellow Card to the Head Coach of Bacolod Masskara as a formal warning following integrity concerns. In May 2026, the league issued a Yellow Card to the Iloilo franchise following similar concerns. In June 2026, the MPBL revoked the franchise of the Iloilo team after violations of league standards. On July 30, 2026, following the July 28 game between Bacolod and Bulacan, the league issued Red Cards, disqualified the individuals involved, and removed the Bacolod Masskara franchise from the remainder of the season. "These actions reflect our commitment to protect the integrity of the MPBL," Oreta said. "If protecting the integrity of this league means having fewer teams, then so be it. I will never compromise the integrity of the MPBL. We owe that to our players, our team owners, our fans, and everyone who believes in fair competition." Beyond the league's administrative actions, the MPBL, through the office of the Chief Legal Counsel, Atty. Glenn Gacal, is in active coordination with the Games and Amusements Board (GAB) and applicable government agencies, such as the National Bureau of Investigation (NBI), to further strengthen the ongoing investigation and pursue the appropriate legal and regulatory actions. Gacal said the MPBL will continue to fully cooperate with the concerned government agencies and provide all necessary assistance to ensure that those responsible are held accountable in accordance with the law. Nobody will be spared from the full-blown investigation, not even team officials and management, that the MBPL is seeking from the GAB, according to Gacal. Regarding the Iloilo franchise, Gacal said rules and regulations, including its sanctions/penalties in the event of breach/violations, are already in place, and the team management's financial obligation to the players and the league should always be timely fulfilled. For Oreta, the message is simple. This is not about one team. It is about protecting every honest player, every team owner, and the credibility of the MPBL. The league will continue to act decisively against anyone who compromises the integrity of the game because the integrity of the MPBL always comes first.

North leans on chemistry, grit in JPGT Finals title defense. Team North heads into the ICTSI Elite Junior PGT Finals fully aware that the road to a second straight title will be far more demanding this time. But while unfamiliarity with the host course presents a formidable obstacle, coach Joey Anciano believes preparation, chemistry and resilience can once again carry his side to victory. Anciano isn't about to reveal too much of his game plan – preferring to keep his strategies close to the vest – but he remains quietly confident that Team North has what it takes to overcome the odds when the Ryder Cup-style championship unfolds from Aug. 18-20 at Pueblo de Oro Golf and Country Club in Cagayan de Oro. Unlike last year's inaugural edition at The Country Club in Santa Rosa, Laguna, where North enjoyed familiar surroundings en route to a convincing 26 1/2–21 1/2 triumph, this year's title defense comes on South territory, where the hosts are expected to capitalize on their greater knowledge of the course. For Anciano, however, local familiarity can only go so far. "Not being familiar with Pueblo de Oro is our biggest challenge," said Anciano. "But golf comes down to execution. To win, we have to start strong, adapt quickly to the layout, and finish strong on every single hole." North's dominant victory a year ago was built on a blistering start. The defending champions swept the opening Four-ball session, 8-4, before edging South, 6 1/2–5 1/2, in the Foursomes to establish a commanding lead. They then held their nerve in the Singles, winning 11 of the 24 matches while halving two others to complete a decisive championship run. Replicating that performance away from home will demand another complete team effort. Anciano believes every point will matter across the boys' and girls' divisions in the 7-10, 11-14 and 15-18 age groups, stressing that no single category can be expected to carry the team. "Since we aren't as familiar with the course layout, we can't rely on just one section," he said. "For us to win, we have to play complete golf from start to finish. Our advantage comes from setting the tone early on the front nine and having the grit to close out strong on the back." The three-day showdown opens with Four-ball matches, where each player plays his or her own ball and the lowest score from each side wins the hole. Day Two features the alternate-shot format before the tournament culminates with the decisive Singles matches on the final day. Organized by Pilipinas Golf Tournaments, Inc., the tournament also serves as a World Amateur Golf Ranking (WAGR)-counting event, bringing together the top 48 junior golfers from the six-leg Luzon (North) and Visayas-Mindanao (South) series in a battle for regional supremacy. Although South appears to hold the advantage of home-course familiarity, North believes its greatest strengths lie elsewhere – in its preparation, shared experience and unwavering belief in one another. "Preparation has been great. Most of our players just got back from the US, but we've managed to sneak in group practices whenever we can," said Anciano. "The good thing is these guys have played together for years. Even though they compete against each other individually, the friendship and camaraderie are really strong. We're locked in and ready." For Team North, defending the title won't simply be about matching last year's dominant performance. It will be about proving that championship golf is defined not by familiarity with the course, but by the ability to adjust, trust one another and deliver when every hole – and every point – matters most.

Manila free surgery program saves woman from 33-year neck tumor. A 73-year-old woman has finally been relieved of a neck tumor she endured for more than three decades after undergoing a successful operation through a free surgery program initiated by a city councilor. Ramona Trinidad, 73, expressed deep gratitude after the tumor, which had been on her neck for about 33 years, was successfully removed. The procedure was made possible through the free surgery program of Joaquin Domagoso , in coordination with doctors and medical staff of the Ospital ng Maynila Medical Center . Trinidad also personally thanked Francisco "Isko Moreno" Domagoso , saying the operation gave her a renewed sense of life and hope. She recalled that she was first noticed during a rice distribution activity, which eventually led to her inclusion in the program. “Buti po nakita niya ako noong magbigayan ng bigas. Akala ko joke lang po ’yung sinabi niya sa akin. Pagdating ng hapon, tinawagan na ako ng staff ninyo. Ang feeling ko po normal na tao na ulit ako (It’s a good thing he saw me during the rice distribution. I thought what he told me was just a joke. By the afternoon, your staff had already called me. I feel like I’m a normal person again),” Trinidad said. “Magpasalamat ka sa Diyos (Give thanks to God)," the mayor told her in response. City officials said the program aims to provide free surgical services to residents who cannot afford medical procedures, particularly those suffering from long-term conditions. The successful operation highlighted the city government’s continuing efforts to expand access to healthcare and deliver essential services to underserved communities.

Vitidsarn, Sonna rule inaugural Philippine International Challenge. Thailand’s Sarunrak Vitidsarn and India’s Ginpaul Sonna made history as the inaugural Philippine International Challenge women’s and men’s singles champions, respectively, as the tournament, presented by the Philippine Sports Commission, concluded on Sunday, Aug. 2, at Gameville Central Park in Mandaluyong City. Both rising stars needed three games to outlast their compatriots in their respective finals and capture their breakthrough International Challenge titles in the tournament backed by the MVP Sports Foundation, Smart, PLDT, Yonex, Sunrise, Maynilad, Cignal, MWell, Jollibee, Milksha, and Telescoop. Vitidsarn weathered a spirited comeback from top seed Tidapron Kleebyeesun before pulling away in the deciding game for a 21–9, 21–23, 21–16 victory after one hour of play, securing her first title at this level. “When I came here, I was really expecting to land at least in the quarterfinals because the past four tournaments I got into the quarterfinals. And in all those tournaments, I lost in the quarterfinals. But when I went past that in this tournament, I took it one by one, point by point,” said the 19-year-old. The younger sister of men's singles world No. 2 Kunlavut Vitidsarn hopes the milestone marks the beginning of carving out her own legacy. “This is my first time winning an IC, so I’m happy and grateful for the hard work I put in, and I thank myself for not giving up,” she added. In the men's singles final, Sonna surged ahead early in the deciding game and never relinquished control, defeating fellow Indian Aryamann Tandon, 25–23, 13–21, 21–16, in a thrilling 55-minute encounter. “For quite a long time I was looking for a good performance, and this is more than expected. I didn’t expect to win this tournament, but it was an exciting process, a way fun one. So, I feel really good winning this competition,” said Sonna, who emerged victorious in the tournament that drew players from 28 countries and was supported by the National Sports Tourism Inter-Agency Committee. After winning titles at home, the 20-year-old from Delhi hopes this long-awaited international triumph serves as a springboard for greater success abroad. “It feels really great to win an international tournament again; it was a valuable experience for me. I just hope to play well and win more tournaments, keep improving, and hope to play better,” Sonna said. India also claimed the women's doubles crown as Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand Pullela rallied past Japan's Miki Kanehiro and Yuna Kato, 16–21, 21–4, 21–17, in the final. Malaysia also collected two titles, with Goh Boon Zhe and Dania Sofia taking the mixed doubles and Choong Hon Jian and Wong Vin Sean winning the men’s doubles. Goh and Sofia finished a comprehensive sweep of Thailand’s Phunawat Horbanluekit and Fungfa Korpthammakit, 21–4, 21–14. Choong and Wong, on the other hand, edged out Indonesia’s Taufik Aderya and Alexius Ongkytama Subagio, 21–16, 13–21, 21–15. Champions in each event received US$1,600, along with a trophy, gold medals, and MWell smartwatches, while the runners-up took home US$960, silver medals, and MWell smartwatches. --// Photos from PBAD

DepEd deploys trauma counselors over Las Pinas school knife attack. The Department of Education has deployed a trauma counseling team for affected learners and staff following the death of a 13-year old high school student who was stabbed dead by his classmate inside a school in Las Piñas City on Friday, July 31. At the same time, DepEd committed support to the family of the victim and cooperation with law enforcement and investigating agencies. “The Department of Education mourns the heartbreaking loss of our learner at Las Piñas National High School Main. We extend our deepest condolences to the family and the entire school community,” the statement read. “Schools must be safe sanctuaries. Violence on our campus is unacceptable and demands accountability and collective action,” it added. On the part of the Philippine National Police (PNP), its chief Gen. Jose Melencio C. Nartatez, Jr, said they will be helping with the DepEd in crafting measures that will focus on holistic approach to address the issue of school violence to protect all the learners and teachers. “We have our coordination, we have our plan, and we are hopeful that we will be able to address this problem to improve the situation, especially on matters involving minors and children in and out of schools,” said Nartatez. Police earlier vowed to extend full assistance to the DepEd, including police visibility in schools and deploying guidance counselors from the PNP’s Women and Children Protection Desk. The PNP also helped in crafting the security and safety protocol during violent incidents and other emergency situations in schools. DepEd, for its part, said they will continue to strengthen partnerships and coordination with other government agencies and stakeholders. “Protecting our youth requires a united effort among schools, families, communities, and law enforcement. We remain relentless in our commitment to restore and uphold our schools as safe spaces for every child,” The DepEd statement read.

Why inclusive education requires more than just a law. By Faye Beatrix Dela Torre co-founder, Stellar Minds PH The Philippines has taken important steps in education reform. Our next challenge is ensuring those reforms become realities inside every classroom. When Republic Act No. 11650, the Inclusive Education for Learners with Disabilities Act, became law in 2022, it affirmed what educators, parents, and advocates have long believed: Every Filipino child deserves the opportunity to learn, participate, and belong. The law was the right call. But every meaningful reform eventually arrives at the same question. The law has been passed. Now what? Education reform is never measured by the number of laws we pass. It is measured by what children experience every day when they walk into a classroom. Children do not experience legislation. They experience classrooms. They experience teachers. They experience whether someone was ready for them. Perhaps that is where the most important conversation about inclusion should begin. From vision to reality The idea behind inclusive education is not new. Its roots can be traced to the disability rights movement of the 1970s. In 1994, the Salamanca Statement brought countries together around a simple but transformative principle: “Schools should accommodate all children, regardless of their physical, intellectual, social, emotional, linguistic or other conditions.” It challenged education systems to rethink one fundamental question: Should children adapt to schools? Or should schools adapt to children? Nearly three decades later, the Philippines embraced that same vision through Republic Act No. 11650. Now, it's time to ask the next question. Not whether inclusion is the right direction because it is. The question now is whether our schools are ready for it. Recently, EDCOM II executive director Dr. Karol Mark Yee reminded us that, “Mainstreaming without preparation is not inclusion.” That statement captures exactly where our national conversation should now go. According to the Second Congressional Commission on Education, the Philippines has an estimated 5.1 million school aged children with disabilities, yet only around 391,000 are enrolled in public schools. Among those enrolled, approximately 60 percent receive no Special Needs Education support, while two out of three teachers report lacking the training and resources needed to effectively support learners with disabilities. These numbers reveal that our greatest challenge is no longer passing legislation. Our greatest challenge is preparing schools to fulfill its promise. Where policy meets the classroom As someone working in education, I have had the privilege of visiting public, private, and international schools across the country. Every visit reminds me that education policy often looks very different once you step inside a classroom. During one school visit, I found myself paying attention to the ordinary things that quietly make learning possible: math manipulatives, visual support, storybooks, picture cards, bond paper, printer ink, and laminating sheets. Most people see classroom supplies. Teachers see opportunities. These are not simply materials. They are the tools that allow teachers to transform one lesson into many because no two children learn in exactly the same way. A visual schedule helps a learner anticipate transitions. Manipulatives turn abstract concepts into something children can see and touch. Picture cards give some learners another way to communicate. A laminated visual may be used hundreds of times across many school years. What appears ordinary often becomes the difference between simply attending a class and truly participating in it. That's when I came to understand that the gap between policy and reality isn't always found in grand projects. Sometimes, it can be found in the simple things that enable a teacher to reach every child. That realization changed the question for me. Instead of asking whether schools are inclusive, perhaps we should ask whether schools have been equipped to become inclusive. A classroom that is ready for every child is not defined by perfection. It is defined by preparation. Preparation means teachers who understand that children learn differently. It means learning environments where children feel safe enough to participate, make mistakes, ask questions, and grow. It means instructional materials that remove barriers instead of expecting every learner to fit the same approach. It means enough time for teachers to observe, assess, collaborate with families, and develop meaningful Individualized Education Programs that become living guides for a child’s learning instead of documents completed for compliance. Most importantly, it means teachers are supported by a team. Inclusive education has never been the responsibility of one person alone.

What it really takes to be a woman in SPAM. The term “Women in SPAM” is all over the internet right now. SPAM stands for social media, public relations, advertising, and marketing, fields often associated with the women many of us grew up watching in hit rom-coms and series such as “The Devil Wears Prada,” “Emily in Paris,” and “Sex and the City.” But there is more to these careers than what we see on screen. Beyond the romanticized image of burnout, overwork, and high-pressure environments, working in SPAM takes grit, creativity, and resilience. To help today's youth understand what it really means to be a woman in SPAM, we asked women leaders in their respective fields what it takes to thrive in the industry. Be willing to learn and start from the bottom. Despite having all the information at your fingertips, it's still important to have a unique voice, point of view, taste, and people skills to survive in this industry. For now, keep reading not just blogs or social media posts but actual books. Get as much information as you can from all sources, get an internship, and train your people skills by joining communities or events whenever you can. Network as early as you can because these connections will help you in the long run. I'm a proud AB Communication graduate, but if there's one thing I wish I had done differently, it would have been to pursue a different field of study in college. Why? Because most of what I apply in my job today wasn't something I learned in the classroom. I learned it through internships, by doing the work, immersing myself in the industry, making mistakes, and figuring things out along the way. One of the mentors I admire most in the SPAM industry actually finished a pre-med course. Imagine that. She didn't build an incredible career because she studied communications; she built it because she brought the discipline, analytical thinking, and rigor that came with studying medicine into everything she did. Succeeding as a woman in the media, PR, advertising, and social media landscapes requires a mindset shift from trying to blend in to unapologetically standing out. The creative industry has historically been male-dominated at the leadership level, but true disruption happens when women leverage their unique perspectives rather than trying to fit into pre-existing corporate molds. Lead with heart and purpose; Embrace emotional storytelling; Protect your creative voice; and build collaborative communities. Work on your writing. Clear, concise, grammatically sound writing is the foundation of effective communications. Re-read “Elements of Style” and “On Writing Well” every year. Work on your presentation. It’s one thing to write well; it’s another thing to present articulately. You will always be in pitch mode, whether to a client, a reader, or a journalist. Practice, practice, practice. Stay updated. This is a fast-moving industry, and things can change overnight. Broaden your reading, build your knowledge, always be curious, and always seek to learn more. Whether your dream is to work in publishing, advertising, public relations, social media, or marketing, a career in SPAM is far more than its glamorous reputation. Behind every viral campaign, magazine cover, or successful brand story are years of learning, collaboration, and perseverance. As these women leaders remind us, succeeding in the industry starts with staying curious, finding your voice, and never being afraid to start from the ground up.

Eala faces grueling turnaround after rain delays DC Open final. Alex Eala faces a tight schedule in her North American hard-court swing after her final match against Jessica Pegula at the rain-delayed Mubadala DC Open in Washington D.C. is rescheduled to Tuesday midnight, Aug. 4 (Philippine time). Eala is scheduled to compete at the National Bank Open in Toronto, Canada which has already started the qualification round. The 21-year-old Filipina is seeded 25th in the WTA 1000 event, a tournament rated just one rung below the Grand Slams. As of press time, Eala has received a first-round bye and is scheduled to open her campaign in the second round on Wednesday night, Aug. 5 (Thursday morning, Aug. 6, PH time), according to the tournament's initial schedule. The tight turnaround would give the Filipina barely more than 24 hours between the conclusion of the Washington final and her opening match in Toronto, leaving little time for recovery and travel. Despite the demanding schedule ahead, Eala remains locked in on her quest for a breakthrough WTA 500 crown in Washington, D.C., where she is making only the second final appearance of her career. Trailing Pegula 4-6, 1-2 when rain halted play, Eala hopes to capitalize on the unexpected layoff as she tries to mount a comeback when the final resumes.

After ‘Luis,’ Typhoon Dolphin to enhance ‘habagat’, bring more rain — PAGASA. Tropical Depression Luis is expected to bring heavy rains over parts of Luzon before weakening, but the country may continue to see significant rainfall as a typhoon internationally called “Dolphin” enhances the southwest monsoon or “habagat,” the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Monday, Aug. 3. In a press conference, PAGASA weather specialist Charmagne Varilla said the heaviest rains on Monday were expected over Pangasinan, where more than 200 millimeters of rainfall (intense to torrential) may be recorded. La Union, Zambales, Tarlac, and Bataan may receive 100 to 200 millimeters of rain (heavy to intense), while southern Cagayan, Cordillera Administrative Region, Ilocos Region, Central Luzon, Metro Manila, Cavite, and Batangas may experience 50 to 100 millimeters of rainfall (moderate to heavy). “Posible ang mga localized flooding and landslide, lalong-lalo na nga sa mga areas na may very high to high susceptibility (Localized flooding and landslides are possible, especially in areas with very high to high susceptibility),” Varilla warned. Luis was last located 180 kilometers east of Echague, Isabela, as of Monday, packing maximum sustained winds of 45 kilometers per hour (kph) and gustiness of up to 55 kph. It was moving northward at 15 kph. Varilla said the tropical depression may turn northwestward in the next few hours and could make landfall over the Cagayan-Isabela area between Monday evening and early Tuesday morning, Aug. 4. After making its closest approach or landfall, Luis is expected to recurve northeastward on Tuesday due to its interaction with Typhoon Dolphin, which remains outside the Philippine Area of Responsibility (PAR). By Wednesday, Varilla said Luis may weaken into a low-pressure area (LPA) or become part of Dolphin's trough and circulation. Wind Signal No. 1 still in effect As of 11 a.m. Monday, Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 1 remains hoisted over the central and eastern portions of Cagayan, Isabela, and Quirino; eastern and southern portions of Apayao; eastern portion of Kalinga; eastern portion of Mountain Province; eastern portion of Ifugao; and northern portion of Aurora. Varilla said the areas under the wind signal were expected to experience minimal impacts, including slight disruptions to daily activities and minimal effects on homes, transportation, agriculture, safety, and telecommunications. The wind signal is expected to remain in effect until Tuesday, with Luis forecast to weaken into an LPA by Wednesday. Typhoon-enhanced ‘habagat’ While Luis is expected to weaken, Dolphin may bring more rain as it enhances the habagat. Varilla said PAGASA has high confidence in the enhancement of the southwest monsoon, with the western section of Luzon expected to be the most affected. “Not only within this week, posible po na magtuloy-tuloy yung habagat po natin hanggang sa succeeding week pa po (Not only within this week, it is possible that the southwest monsoon may continue into the succeeding week),” Varilla said. The habagat is expected to bring significant rains to more areas as Luis moves away. From Tuesday noon to Wednesday noon, significant rainfall may persist over most of Central Luzon and the western section of Northern Luzon, including La Union, Pangasinan, Zambales, Tarlac, and Bataan. Occidental Mindoro may also receive significant rains due to the habagat. By Wednesday noon to Thursday noon, Aug. 6, the habagat is expected to affect the entire country, with significant rains still possible over Zambales, Bataan, Cavite, Batangas, Occidental Mindoro, and Antique. “Muli, mas i-emphasize po natin yung magiging epekto ng malalakas na mga pag-ulan na dadalhin ng habagat at nung si Bagyong Luis (Again, we want to emphasize the effects of the heavy rains that will be brought by the southwest monsoon and Typhoon Luis),” Varilla said. ‘Dolphin’ unlikely to make landfall Typhoon Dolphin was last located 2,735 kilometers east-northeast of extreme Northern Luzon, packing maximum sustained winds of 155 kph and gustiness of up to 190 kph. It may enter the PAR in the coming days but has a low chance of making landfall in the country, Varilla said. “Kung papasok man, more on dito lang sa may northern periphery ng ating PAR. Ngunit, wala itong direktang epekto sa alinmang bahagi ng ating bansa (If it enters, it will likely remain over the northern periphery of our PAR. However, it will have no direct impact on any part of our country),” she said.

Economic diplomacy shines at WOFEX. When Polish Minister of Agriculture and Rural Development Stefan Krajewski arrived in Manila, he wasn’t simply promoting dairy products, meat, confectionery, and apples. He was making a diplomatic case for why more Polish food deserves a place on Filipino tables. His visit marked Poland’s first-ever national pavilion at the World Food Expo (WOFEX), the country’s largest food and hospitality trade exhibition. It also placed Poland among a diverse group of countries that used this year’s expo to showcase their national food industries and deepen commercial engagement with the Philippines. Poland’s participation was among the week’s biggest milestones. Organized by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development together with the National Support Centre for Agriculture (KOWR), the “Poland Tastes Good” national pavilion brought together 11 leading Polish food manufacturers showcasing dairy products, poultry, pork, processed meats, confectionery, snacks, and food ingredients. During a recent interview with Filipino journalists in Warsaw, Krajewski described the Philippines as one of Southeast Asia’s most promising food markets and emphasized Poland’s commitment to building long-term partnerships with Filipino importers and consumers. His visit to Manila translated that commitment into action, combining government-to-government engagement with business matching sessions and direct meetings between Polish exporters and Philippine buyers. For Poland, WOFEX represented an opportunity to introduce the country’s food industry to a market where bilateral agricultural trade continues to grow, particularly as the Philippines and the European Union move closer to a Free Trade Agreement. Norway, meanwhile, demonstrated the value of consistency. This year marked the fourth consecutive Norwegian Seafood Pavilion jointly organized by the Royal Norwegian Embassy in Manila and the Norwegian Seafood Council, reflecting the country’s sustained investment in the Philippine market. Welcoming guests to the Norwegian reception, First Secretary Øystein Bell noted that each year has brought growing interest in Norwegian seafood and stronger partnerships with the Philippine food industry. “This gives us great confidence that the market for Norwegian seafood in the Philippines will continue to grow in the years ahead,” he said. Bell also highlighted how Norwegian salmon has evolved beyond sushi and sashimi to become part of Filipino cuisine itself. “For many years, it has been enjoyed in sinigang,” he said. “More recently, chefs have been giving traditional dishes a modern twist by using Norwegian salmon in favorites such as Bicol Express and sisig.” The Philippines’ growing appetite for Norwegian seafood is also being felt by exporters. “I’m very happy to be back in the Philippines once again,” said Federico Ovati of Norwegian company Seafood Brands. “It’s incredibly rewarding to see how the efforts we’ve invested over the past few years are delivering such positive results. The Philippine market continues to grow rapidly, and consumer demand for high-quality Norwegian salmon and trout keeps increasing.” Canada likewise mounted one of the exhibition’s strongest official country presences through a coordinated Team Canada approach. The Embassy of Canada, Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada, Canada Beef, Canada Pork, and Canadian exporters joined forces to promote Canadian food products and strengthen commercial ties with Philippine importers. Elsewhere across the exhibition floor, government-backed participation underscored how food has become an increasingly important component of economic diplomacy. South Korea’s pavilion promoted Korean food products as part of the country’s continuing global K-food campaign, while Thailand’s Trade Center Manila supported Thai exporters seeking new business opportunities in the Philippines. Spain highlighted its premium beef industry through the European Beef from Spain campaign, while Malaysia showcased Halal food manufacturers as part of its broader efforts to expand halal and processed food exports across Southeast Asia. The United States also maintained a strong official presence through the US Department of Agriculture, the US Meat Export Federation, and the USA Poultry & Egg Export Council, reflecting the longstanding importance of agricultural trade in the broader US-Philippines economic relationship. Brazil, one of the world’s largest exporters of animal protein, likewise reinforced its position through industry associations and exporters promoting Brazilian beef and poultry products. Viewed individually, each pavilion represented a country promoting its products. Taken together, they illustrated something much larger. Trade exhibitions such as WOFEX have increasingly become platforms for economic diplomacy, where embassies work alongside exporters, government agencies, and industry groups to strengthen commercial relationships that ultimately support broader bilateral ties. For diplomats, food has become more than a cultural calling card. It is an export, an investment opportunity, and increasingly, an instrument of economic statecraft. Long before free trade agreements are signed or major investments announced, relationships often begin over a shared meal. At WOFEX, that simple idea was on display throughout the exhibition halls, where every national pavilion offered both a taste of home and a warm invitation to do business.

Seo In Guk returning to Manila this August. South Korean actor and singer Seo In Guk is set to return to the Philippines this month for a special public appearance in Manila. The Korean star will headline an event at the Main Atrium of SM Mall of Asia on Aug. 22. Ticketing mechanics and other event details have yet to be announced. Seo's upcoming visit marks his return to the Philippines more than a year after his February 2025 trip, when he was introduced as one of the country's tourism ambassadors. During that visit, the Korean star explored Boracay for the first time, where he experienced the island's popular crystal kayak attraction. He also met Filipino fans during a fan event in Manila. Seo rose to international fame through hit Korean dramas including "Reply 1997," "The Master's Sun," and "Hello Monster." He has since built a successful career as both an actor and recording artist. Aside from starring in television dramas, Seo has lent his voice to several K-drama original soundtracks, with songs such as "My Love," "All for You," and "Distant Fate" gaining popularity among fans.

Romeo Jalosjos, TV producer behind 'Eat Bulaga!' and TAPE Inc., dies at 85. Former television producer Romeo "Nonong" Garcia Jalosjos, one of the key figures behind the success of the long-running noontime program "Eat Bulaga!," has died. He was 85. His son, Seth Frederick "Bullet" Jalosjos, announced the news in a statement posted on social media on Sunday, Aug. 2. "It is with profound sorrow and heavy hearts that our family announces the passing of our beloved father, Romeo 'Nonong' Garcia Jalosjos," Bullet wrote. The family has not disclosed the cause of death. According to the announcement, Jalosjos' wake will be held at The Heritage Park in Taguig City from Aug. 3 to Aug. 5 before his remains are brought to Dapitan City, Zamboanga del Norte, where funeral services will continue from Aug. 6 to Aug. 12. In his tribute, Bullet remembered his father as a media pioneer, visionary, and devoted family man whose work left a lasting mark on both the television industry and public service. "While we grieve his passing, we also celebrate a life lived with extraordinary purpose," he said, adding that his father's legacy would live on through the people he inspired and the communities he helped build. Jalosjos was best known in the entertainment industry as one of the founders of Television and Production Exponents Inc. (TAPE Inc.), which he established with veteran producer Tony Tuviera in 1981. Under TAPE, the company produced "Eat Bulaga!" for more than four decades, helping turn it into the country's longest-running noontime variety show and one of Philippine television's most enduring entertainment brands. Long before TAPE was formed, Jalosjos worked as a television producer for ABC and ABS-CBN, making him one of the industry's early behind-the-scenes figures before martial law was declared in 1972. Beyond television, Jalosjos also ventured into politics, serving as congressman for Zamboanga del Norte. His political career, however, ended after his conviction in a high-profile criminal case that was later affirmed by the Supreme Court. He also made headlines over the years for his ties to the entertainment industry, including his relationship with the late actress Nida Blanca before marrying former singer Lourna Pal. Jalosjos is survived by his family, who thanked the public for their prayers, condolences, and support as they mourn his passing.

Palace unfazed by China's objections, new rules over Bajo de Masinloc. Malacañang appeared unfazed by China's objections and new rules covering Bajo de Masinloc, saying the Philippines would continue asserting its rights based on its own laws, the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS), and the landmark 2016 South China Sea Arbitral Award. Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said this following China's condemnation of the Philippines' baselines around Bajo de Masinloc after Manila formally deposited with the United Nations its official nautical chart showing the baselines and surrounding maritime zones of the shoal. In a press briefing on Monday, Aug. 3, Castro maintained that China's rejection of Manila's legal position would not change the Marcos administration's approach of defending the country's maritime rights through peaceful, diplomatic, and legal means. "Tayo lamang, ang Pangulo, at ang administrasyon ay tumutupad kung ano ang sinasabi ng ating batas, kung ano ang sinasabi ng UNCLOS at kung ano ang nasabi na sa arbitral ruling (The President and the administration are simply complying with what our laws provide, what UNCLOS provides, and what has been stated in the arbitral ruling)," she said. Castro said the Philippines will not claim a territory that it doesn’t own. "Hindi tayo lalagpas diyan, hindi tayo mang-aangkin ng teritoryo, ng anumang karapatan ng iba (We will not go beyond that, and we will not claim the territory or rights of others),” she said. “Ang ipinaglalaban lang ng ating pamahalaan ay kung ano ang nasa atin, kung ano ang sinasabi ng batas, kung ano ang sinasabi ng arbitral ruling at ng UNCLOS (Our government is only fighting for what belongs to us, what the law provides, and what the arbitral ruling and UNCLOS say)," she added. China’s nature reserve rules Asked about China's recently released implementing rules for its declared nature reserve at Bajo de Masinloc, the Palace Press Officer stressed that Beijing's domestic rules would not override the Philippines' own laws and maritime entitlements. "Batas nila iyan pero mayroon tayong sariling batas—batas natin na puwede ding ipatupad at ang batas natin ay naaayon sa UNCLOS, sa sarili nating batas, sa sarili nating pagkilala, pati na rin ang arbitral ruling (Those are their laws, but we have our own laws—laws that we can also enforce, and our laws are consistent with UNCLOS, our own laws, our own recognition, as well as the arbitral ruling)," Castro said. "So, wala tayong nilalabag na anumang batas at wala tayong inaangking anumang teritoryo (So, we are not violating any law, and we are not claiming any territory that does not belong to us)," she added. The rules reportedly provide for routine patrols within China's declared nature reserve at the shoal, impose penalties for violations, and require prior approval before certain activities may be conducted within the area. China announced the establishment of what it calls the Huangyan Dao National Nature Reserve at Bajo de Masinloc as Beijing continues to assert sovereignty and administrative control over the shoal despite Manila's rejection of its claims. China rejects PH baselines Beijing earlier rejected the Philippines' delimitation of territorial sea baselines around Bajo de Masinloc, describing the move as a "grave infringement" of Chinese sovereignty and a violation of international law, including UNCLOS. China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs declared the Philippine baselines "illegal, null, and void," and warned Manila to refrain from what it described as infringement and provocation around the shoal or face a "resolute" response from Beijing. The Chinese government maintains that Bajo de Masinloc, which it calls Huangyan Dao, is its "inherent territory" and has likewise rejected the Philippines' Maritime Zones Act and the 2016 Arbitral Award. The 2016 tribunal, however, ruled that there was no legal basis for China's sweeping claims to historic rights within its so-called "nine-dash line" under UNCLOS, while finding that Bajo de Masinloc is a high-tide feature capable of generating a 12-nautical-mile territorial sea but not an exclusive economic zone or continental shelf of its own. The tribunal also found that Filipino and Chinese fishermen had traditional fishing rights at the shoal and that China had unlawfully prevented Filipino fishermen from engaging in traditional fishing there beginning in May 2012. PH deposits chart with UN The latest exchange came after the Philippines formally deposited with the UN Secretariat on July 29 its official nautical chart of Bajo de Masinloc and its surrounding maritime zones, placing Manila's baseline information on the public international record. The Department of Foreign Affairs (DFA) said National Mapping and Resource Information Authority Chart No. 1567, entitled "Bajo de Masinloc and Approach," depicts the normal baselines of the shoal, together with the outer limits of its territorial sea and contiguous zone, in accordance with UNCLOS and Philippine law. According to the DFA, the Philippines maintains under the Maritime Zones Act, UNCLOS, and the 2016 Arbitral Award that Bajo de Masinloc generates a territorial sea extending up to 12 nautical miles from its normal baselines and a contiguous zone extending from 12 to 24 nautical miles. The deposit followed another Philippine move at the United Nations in which Manila formally presented before the UN Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf its partial submission concerning the country's entitlement to an extended continental shelf in the West Philippine Sea covering the West Palawan Region. Palace backs Teodoro Meanwhile, Malacañang backed Department of National Defense (DND) Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr.’s remarks that elected officials siding with China's position on the West Philippine Sea should consider resigning because they had sworn to uphold the Constitution and Philippine laws. Castro said the Marcos administration saw nothing wrong with Teodoro's remarks, stressing that defending Philippine interests should be separate from maintaining economic and diplomatic relations with China. "Totoo na mayroon tayong magandang relasyon sa China patungkol sa trade, investment, negosyo—hindi iyan usapin (We indeed have good relations with China when it comes to trade, investment, and business—that is not the issue),” she said. “So, hindi puwedeng pagsamahin ang pagnenegosyo, magandang relasyon sa China sa pagpoprotekta sa interes ng Pilipinas (So, business and good relations with China cannot be conflated with protecting Philippine interests)," she added. Castro also described as "very alarming" Davao City Rep. Paolo "Pulong" Duterte's criticism that Teodoro appeared to be imposing a loyalty test, saying Filipinos should put the country's interests first. She said it would be better if all officials who are siding with China came out in the open. "Mas maganda po siguro talaga kung kayo po ay nagpapakita ng katulad na pananaw ni Congressman Pulong Duterte, mas magandang lumantad na sila para makita natin kung sino ba talaga ang totoong nagmamahal sa bansang Pilipinas (Perhaps it would be better if those who share views similar to Congressman Pulong Duterte would come out in the open so we can see who truly loves the Philippines)," Castro said.

'No stipulation': VP Sara's camp denies spending P125-M confidential fund in 11 days. The defense team of Vice President Sara Duterte on Monday, August 3, rejected the prosecution's assertion that the Office of the Vice President (OVP) spent its P125 million confidential fund within 11 days in December 2022, disputing a claim based on Commission on Audit (COA) records during the 11th day of the Senate impeachment trial. Defense lawyer Michael Poa refused to stipulate to the prosecution's proposed admission that the OVP received the P125 million confidential fund on Dec. 20, 2022, and fully disbursed it within 11 days, as reflected in COA records. "No stipulation on this matter," Poa told the Senate impeachment court. The issue is being tackled under Article I of the Articles of Impeachment, which accuses Duterte of misusing P612.5 million in confidential funds allocated to the OVP and the Department of Education (DepEd) during her tenure as Education secretary. In legal proceedings, a stipulation is a “formal agreement between opposing parties in a case to accept a fact, document, or issue as true or valid without requiring further proof.” By contrast, a "no stipulation" means one party refuses to admit or accept the proposed fact or evidence, requiring it to be proven at trial. Defense acknowledges fund allocation, not alleged 11-day spending While rejecting the prosecution's proposed stipulation on the alleged 11-day utilization of the confidential fund, Poa acknowledged that the OVP was allocated P125 million in confidential funds in 2022. He added, however, that the release of the amount had been approved by President Ferdinand "Bongbong" Marcos Jr., a point acknowledged by prosecution counsel Lorna Kapunan. The prosecution sought to establish that the OVP received the confidential fund on Dec. 20, 2022, and liquidated it within 11 days, based on COA records. The issue first drew public attention during the 2024 national budget deliberations in September 2023, when then-Marikina Rep. Stella Quimbo, who served as sponsor of the COA budget, disclosed that the OVP's liquidation report showed the confidential fund had been utilized within 11 days—not 19 days, as initially computed by members of the Makabayan bloc. Quimbo said the liquidation report had been submitted by the OVP to the COA in January 2023. The COA later issued a Notice of Disallowance covering P73 million of the P125 million confidential fund, citing alleged violations of the 2015 Joint Circular governing the allowable use of confidential funds. Acknowledgment receipts questioned Aside from disputing the prosecution's proposed stipulation on the confidential fund timeline, the defense also raised concerns over several acknowledgment receipts presented as evidence. Poa told the impeachment court that the defense was willing to stipulate to most of the prosecution's documentary evidence but would exclude acknowledgment receipts covering Dec. 21 to 31, 2022. "The defense is willing to stipulate on the list of documents provided except for the acknowledgment receipts for the period covering December 21 to 31, 2022," Poa said. He added that there were issues involving those receipts that would be addressed by future witnesses but did not elaborate on the specific concerns. Before raising the objection, Poa requested a brief suspension of the proceedings to coordinate with the prosecution regarding the documents both sides intended to stipulate. "We have no problem stipulating, but due to the voluminous nature of the documents, we just want to make sure while ensuring the rights of our client," he said. Article I hearings continue The discussion on document stipulations formed part of the Senate impeachment court's proceedings on Article I, which centers on allegations that Duterte misused confidential funds entrusted to both the OVP and the DepEd. The defense maintained that it needed to thoroughly examine the extensive documentary evidence before agreeing to any stipulations, arguing that such a review was necessary to safeguard the Duterte’s rights as the impeachment trial proceeds.

Gov’t to fight for P85 NCR wage hike amid court TRO—Palace. The Marcos administration will fight to implement the P85 daily minimum wage increase in Metro Manila after a court issued a temporary restraining order (TRO) against the new wage order, Malacañang said Monday, Aug. 3. Presidential Communications Office (PCO) Undersecretary Claire Castro said the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) is ready to defend Wage Order No. NCR-27, which granted the increase to minimum wage earners in the National Capital Region (NCR). “Ang Office of the Solicitor General ay ready naman po na ipaglaban po ang wage order na naipasa po para sa ating mga manggagawa (The Office of the Solicitor General is ready to fight for the wage order that was passed for our workers),” she said in a Palace press briefing. Castro said the government respects the courts but maintains its right to defend what it believes is appropriate for workers, adding that documents and objections are already being prepared in response to the TRO. “Sa ngayon po ay mayroon na pong ginagawa po na dokumento at pagtutol, although, of course, iginagalang natin ang lahat ng korte (At present, documents and objections are already being prepared, although, of course, we respect all courts),” she said. “Pero ang pamahalaan, ang administrasyon, ay mayroon naman din pong karapatan na ihayag kung ano ang nararapat para sa ating mga kababayan at sa ating mga manggagawa (However, the government, the administration, also has the right to express what is appropriate for our fellow Filipinos and our workers),” she said. The Palace Press Officer also said the proper remedy for anyone questioning the wage adjustment should have been to file an appeal through the regional wage-setting mechanism instead of going to court. Asked whether the wage increase could be implemented after the 20-day TRO expires on Aug. 13, Castro declined to speculate, saying the Palace would not preempt the court or the OSG. “Sa ngayon po ay ipinaglalaban ang stance ng ating pamahalaan patungkol sa wage order para sa ating mga kababayan sa NCR (For now, the government is fighting for its position regarding the wage order for our fellow Filipinos in the NCR),” she said. Wage Order No. NCR-27 grants a total P85 daily minimum wage increase in two tranches, with P60 intended to take effect on July 25 and the remaining P25 on Jan. 20, 2027, bringing the minimum daily wage for non-agriculture workers from P695 to P780 upon full implementation. The Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) earlier said more than 1.1 million minimum wage earners in Metro Manila would directly benefit from the adjustment, which it described as the largest single daily minimum wage increase approved in the region. President Marcos has also said regional wage boards are continuously reviewing economic conditions in their respective areas to determine whether workers outside Metro Manila should receive salary adjustments, with decisions in several regions expected later this year. Legislated wage hike Asked whether the TRO could prompt Marcos to support calls for a legislated wage hike instead, Castro said the President wants workers to receive appropriate wages but that the government would continue working through the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Boards unless Congress passes a law providing otherwise. “Ang pagbibigay naman po nang tamang wage or suweldo sa ating mga manggagawa ito naman po ay nais ng Pangulo, kaya hangga’t wala pang nagagawa na batas patungkol po dito tuluy-tuloy po ang pagtatrabaho ng pamahalaan at ng Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board para po matugunan ang pangangailangan ng ating mga kababayan (The President wants our workers to receive the proper wage or salary, so as long as there is no law on this matter, the government and the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board will continue working to address the needs of our fellow Filipinos),” she said. The Palace had taken a similar position in June 2025 amid proposals in Congress for a P200 across-the-board wage increase, with Castro saying that any legislated increase would have to come from Congress. “‘Yan po ay nasa Kongreso (That lies with Congress),” she said at the time. “Hindi po pwedeng basta magdikta ang Pangulo (The President cannot just dictate),” she added. Castro had also stressed that Marcos was not opposed to higher wages, pointing to increases approved through the regional wage boards. “Taun-taon po, ‘yan po ang hiling ng Pangulo—na magkaroon po ng pagtaas ng sweldo (Every year, the President calls for salary increases),” she said.

A suicide bomber strikes an antimilitant rally in northwestern Pakistan, killing at least 14. PESHAWAR, Pakistan (AP) — A suicide bomber targeted protesters at an antimilitant rally in northwestern Pakistan on Sunday, killing at least 14 people, mostly civilians and police officers, and wounding more than two dozen others, officials said. The attack happened in Kabal, a town in Swat Valley in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, where demonstrators had gathered near a police station, chanting antimilitant slogans and demanding peace, district police chief Omar Khan said. According to witnesses, shortly before the attack, speakers at the rally said that ensuring security and eliminating militancy were the state’s responsibility. They also accused authorities of failing to act decisively against militants, saying residents wanted to live without fear after years of violence that devastated the region. Bilal Faizi, a spokesman for the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provincial emergency service, said the attacker struck dozens of people who were chanting antimilitant slogans and demanding peace. Police official Omar Khan said at least nine civilians and five officers were among the dead. President and prime minister offer condolences Pakistan’s President Asif Ali Zardari and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the bombing, expressing deep sorrow over the loss of life. In separate statements they offered condolences to the families of those killed, prayed for the recovery of the wounded and directed authorities to ensure the wounded receive the best possible medical treatment. Zardari and Sharif also said Pakistan’s fight against terrorism would continue until it is eradicated. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also condemned the attack. In a statement, he extending condolences to the families of those killed and prayers for the speedy recovery of the wounded. The Swat Valley was once a stronghold of Islamic militants who imposed a strict interpretation of Sharia, or Islamic law, before the Pakistani military launched a major operation in 2007 that drove them out and restored government control. However, militants have resurfaced in Pakistan’s Swat Valley in recent months, fueling fears that the Pakistani Taliban are seeking to regain a foothold in the region. In response, residents have repeatedly staged anti-Taliban rallies to protest the militants’ presence across the valley. Suspicion falls on Pakistani Taliban No group immediately claimed responsibility for the bombing, but suspicion is likely to fall on the Pakistani Taliban, known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP. The TTP is separate from, but allied with, Afghanistan’s Taliban rulers. Many of its leaders and fighters have found sanctuary in Afghanistan since the Taliban returned to power there in 2021. Pakistan has long accused Afghanistan’s Taliban government of harboring TTP militants, an allegation Kabul denies. Pakistan has experienced a surge in militant attacks in recent years, particularly targeting police and security forces. On Friday, Pakistan's military spokesman Ahmad Sharif Chaudhry said that Pakistan has recorded 3,145 “terrorism incidents” since January. He said Pakistan had killed 2,084 militants since January, while 819 Pakistanis, including soldiers, police officers and civilians, had been killed. Chaudhry also said Afghanistan-based militants had carried out 28 suicide attacks in Pakistan since January and alleged that most were carried out by Afghan nationals or people associated with Afghanistan’s security forces. He said the TTP and other militant groups were carrying out attacks inside Pakistan with the support of Afghanistan’s Taliban rulers and Pakistan would continue to target the TTP and its support infrastructure.

Angat Dam slowly recovering from record-low water level, PAGASA says. The water level of Angat Dam in Bulacan has recovered nearly five meters from its record-low elevation last week, with further increases possible as rains continue over its watershed, the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA) said on Monday, Aug. 3. The dam's water level rose to 155.41 meters as of 8 a.m. Monday, up nearly five meters from the 150.6-meter record-low on July 25. During a press conference, Engr. Socrates Paat Jr., chief of the PAGASA Hydrometeorology Division, said the dam's elevation has been rising, although the recovery has not been steady. “Umangat ang elevation ng Angat for more than a week na (The elevation of Angat has been rising for more than a week),” Paat said, citing the recent rains that have helped raise the dam's water level. “Dahil mataas ang confidence natin sa mga pag-ulan, malakas din ang possibility na aangat pa further yung elevation ng Angat Dam (Because we have high confidence in the occurrence of rains, there is also a strong possibility that the elevation of Angat Dam will rise further),” Paat said. READ MORE: mb.com.ph/2026/08/03/after-luis-typhoon-dolphin-to-enhance-habagat-bring-more-rain-pagasa PAGASA hydrologist Jofren Habaluyas said the dam's water level nevertheless dropped by 0.04 meters over the past 24 hours. He said the dam has shown an increasing trend over the past three to four days, which could be due to the condition of the Angat watershed. “So tinitignan namin based sa aming analysis, possible na baka yung watershed ng Angat is saturated na. So kung ano man na yung rainfall na ma-receive is madali yung magiging reaction or translation niya dito sa storage ng tubig sa dam (Based on our analysis, it is possible that the Angat watershed is already saturated. So whatever rainfall it receives will quickly translate into additional water stored in the dam),” Habaluyas said. However, the dam's current level remains 24.93 meters below the 180.34-meter rule curve elevation, which represents the level at which Angat Dam is considered to be under normal operations. Habaluyas said about 470 millimeters of rainfall would be needed for the dam to reach the rule curve elevation. Paat, however, cautioned the public against becoming complacent as Angat Dam remains below the rule curve. He said the dam's water level is expected to continue rising, although the increase may not be substantial. “Patuloy tayo magtipid sa tubig para itong mga nababawi na ating mga increases in water level na ito ay hindi mabilis ang pagdeplete (We should continue conserving water so that these gains in water level will not be quickly depleted),” Paat said.

COA witness says VP Sara signed liquidation report for P125-M confidential fund-cash advance. Impeachment trial respondent Vice President Sara Duterte signed the Office of the Vice President’s (OVP) liquidation report certifying that the purpose of its P125-million confidential fund-cash advance had been accomplished, Prosecution witness Commission on Audit (COA) auditor Roderick Wamil gave this testimony before senator-judges Monday, Aug. 3 during day 11 of the Senate impeachment trial. This was in continuation of the litigation on article I of the four articles of impeachment, which covered the alleged misuse of P612.5 million worth of confidential funds on the part of the respondent. Wamil--during direct examination by prosecutor Lorna Kapunan--identified Duterte’s signature on the related disbursement voucher, accomplishment report, and an OVP certification. On the disbursement voucher, Wamil said Duterte certified matters concerning the legality of the cash advance and its expenditure under her direct supervision. Asked to identify the signature appearing above Duterte’s name, Wamil answered: “That is the signature po of the Vice President Sara Duterte.” Kapunan then showed Wamil a liquidation report dated Jan. 10, 2023. The document carried a certification that the purpose of the cash advance had been duly accomplished. “Ang significance po nung kanyang pirma dito ay kanya pong sinertify na ’yung purpose po nung kanilang cash advance from the confidential fund ay na-accomplish po ng agency,” Wamil explained. (The significance of his signature here is that he certified the purpose of their cash advance from the confidential fund was accomplished by the agency.) P125 million in 11 days The liquidation report covered the period from Dec. 21 to 31, 2022. Wamil said the underlying Physical and Financial Plan indicated that the cash advance was intended for the entire fourth quarter, covering October through December. “Based on this document po, na-disburse lang siya (it was disbursed) from December 21 to 31, 2022, or around 11 days,” he told the court. Wamil said the documents placed the amount involved at P125 million. He clarified that the 11-day period came from the OVP’s own liquidation report. The OVP's alleged spending of P125 million in just 11 days has been among the more persistent allegations of wrongdoing against Duterte ever since she was first impeached by the House in 2025. Kapunan next presented the OVP accomplishment report submitted to COA’s Intelligence and Confidential Fund Audit Office. Wamil again identified Duterte’s signature, this time beneath the words “approved by”. “It signifies po that the signatory, or the Vice President, approved the contents of this accomplishment report,” Wamil said. At any rate, the COA witness found that the accomplishment report "did not enumerate the specific confidential activities" undertaken by the OVP. He said such details were necessary for COA to determine whether the expenditures fell within the allowable purposes listed under Item 4.8 of Joint Circular No. 2015-01. A separate OVP certification bore Duterte’s signature under the word “attested". Wamil explained the significance of that notation in the audit. “Ang ibig sabihin po ng ‘attested’ ay kanyang kino-confirm at bine-verify na ’yung contents nung certification na ito ay totoo,” he said. ('Attested’ means she is confirming and verifying that the contents of this certification are true.) Wamil observed that the certification was dated Jan. 10, 2022 even though it was pertaining to a cash advance for the fourth quarter of 2022 and was notarized on Jan. 16, 2023. He described this as a discrepancy in the dates but expressly said his team found no other violation in that certification because the required form had been submitted. “After the evaluation of those documents, since I noted that the documents are not compliant with the requirements of Joint Circular 2015-01, I drafted an Audit Observation Memorandum,” Wamil said. The audit was based on the full set of OVP liquidation documents rather than one record in isolation. 15 boxes Monday's Senate impeachment trial began with the visual of 15 boxes of documentary evidence being hauled to the session hall. The boxes were marked with the words "confidential funds". "Your Honors, please, as you can see in front of you, we have 15 boxes, 15 boxes of confidential fund [records],” Kapunan told the court. She said the records consisted of liquidation documents submitted by the OVP. and the Department of Education (DepEd) to the COA in support of the liquidation of their confidential funds. Duterte served as DepEd secretary from 2022 to 2024.
