The documents cover P500 million in OVP confidential funds for the fourth quarter of 2022 and the first three quarters of 2023, and P112.5 million in DepEd confidential funds for the first three quarters of 2023. This totalled to P612.5 million. Many of the records are expected to relate to the liquidation documents examined during the House Committee on Good Government and Public Accountability’s 2024 inquiry into Duterte’s confidential funds. That investigation uncovered acknowledgment receipts bearing names such as “Mary Grace Piattos,” “Milky Sekuya” and “Kokoy Villamin", which were purportedly among the fictitious recipients used to justify confidential fund disbursements . It also cited Philippine Statistics Authority (PSA) certifications showing no matching birth records for many listed recipients and National Bureau of Investigation (NBI) findings that several acknowledgment receipts appeared to have been signed by the same hand.

PH disputes China's claim of Scarborough combat drills, says reports ‘not credible’. The national government on Monday, Aug. 3, rejected China’s announcement that it carried out joint naval and air combat exercises around Bajo de Masinloc or Scarbororugh Shoal (Panatag Shoal) in the West Philippine Sea (WPS), saying available monitoring by security agencies did not support the claim. National Maritime Council (NMC) spokesperson Undersecretary Alexander Lopez said reports from the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) and the Philippine Coast Guard (PCG) showed the continued presence of Chinese vessels in the area but did not detect the activities described by China. “Based on currently available reporting, the report that China conducted a joint naval-air combat patrol around Bajo de Masinloc on Aug. 1, 2026 was deemed not credible,” said Lopez, a retired admiral. “As per monitoring and reports from our AFP and PCG units, there is a presence of China Coast Guard, maritime militia, and People's Liberation Army-Navy (PLA-N) vessels at Bajo de Masinloc, as monitored and reported on a daily basis,” he continued. “But as to the actual conduct of navy-air combat drills, there were no such activities. This is again Chinese propaganda to ‘assert’ their maritime claims and support their activities over Bajo de Masinloc,” he added. 'Drills can't alter facts' The People's Liberation Army (PLA) Southern Theater Command announced on Aug. 1 that it had conducted joint naval and air exercises in and around Scarborough Shoal, known locally as Bajo de Masinloc, located 124 nautical miles from the coast of Zambales, within the 200 nautical mile exclusive economic zone (EEZ) of the country, and about 472 nautical miles from Hainan, the nearest point in China. Chinese state media reported that the drills involved H-6K bombers armed with YJ-12 supersonic anti-ship missiles, guided missile frigates, helicopters, amphibious vessels, and China Coast Guard ships carrying out interception, boarding, inspection, and towing operations. China announced the exercises days after Manila submitted to the United Nations (UN) its bid to extend its continental shelf beyond the country's 200-nautical-mile EEZ off Palawan. The national government also deposited its official nautical chart of Bajo de Masinloc with the UN. Beijing rejected both moves, describing them as illegal and insisting on its claim over the disputed shoal. It also urged the UN Commission on the Limits of the Continental Shelf not to act on the Philippine submission. Despite China's statements, Lopez said military activities cannot change ownership or maritime entitlements under international law. “Be that as it may, even if China does conduct naval and air patrols around Bajo de Masinloc, such activities do not alter the legal status of the area, based on international law, including UNCLOS [United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS) and the 2016 Arbitral Award. Bajo de Masinloc remains an integral part of Philippine territory and the Philippines exercises sovereignty and sovereign rights over the maritime zones that surround it,” he said. “It is important to note that military drills cannot create sovereignty or maritime rights under international law,” he added. Continuous monitoring The NMC said the government will continue monitoring developments in the area while considering diplomatic action based only on verified information. “Any military drills at Bajo de Masinloc are deemed illegal and can pose security and safety issues to civilian shipping, air traffic, and fishing activities in the area. Diplomatic actions will be based on verified reports coming from our operational units, including the AFP, PCG, and BFAR [Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources],” Lopez said. Scarborough Shoal has remained one of the main flashpoints in the South China Sea, with repeated confrontations between Philippine and Chinese vessels. The dispute continues despite the 2016 arbitral ruling that invalidated China's sweeping claims in the South China Sea, a decision Beijing continues to reject.

Religious leader killed in Agusan del Sur ambush. BUTUAN CITY – A religious leader was killed and a tribal member was wounded in an ambush in Barangay Rizal, San Francisco, Agusan del Sur on Friday afternoon, July 31. Police identified the fatality as Pastor Balvino Andaya, 61, a leader of the Risen Christ Community Church, and the wounded as Avelino Cajandig, 59, a member of the Banwaon Manobo Talaandig Tribal Council (BAMATA-TC). Investigation said the victims were traveling aboard a Mitsubishi Montero Sport from Barangay Del Monte, Talacogon, Agusan del Sur when two unidentified motorcycle-riding suspects opened fire at their vehicle. The Sports Utility Vehicle veered off the road and crashed into a roadside sari-sari store. The Police Regional Office-13 on Monday ordered an extensive investigation of the incident and manhunt against the suspects. A case conference was held at the San Francisco Municipal Police Station (MPS) led by PRO-13 Director Police Brig. Gen. Marcial Mariano P. Magistrado IV where investigators presented updates on the circumstances surrounding the incident, evidence gathered, intelligence developments, and the progress of ongoing investigative and follow-up operations. Andaya died from multiple bullet wounds. Cajandig sustained a bullet wound and being treated in an undisclosed hospital. Recovered from the area were several fired cartridge cases and fired bullets. These pieces of evidence were submitted for forensic and ballistic examinations PRO-13 Public Information Office chief Police Lt. Col. Jennifer S. Ometer said hot-pursuit and follow-up operations are in full swing. “Our ground personnel are in round-the-clock operation to solve this incident,” Ometer added. Magistrado activated “Oplan: Cure” to further strengthen operational support and sustain the manhunt for the perpetrators. “We assure the public that PRO-13 is exhausting all available investigative and intelligence resources to ensure the immediate identification and arrest of those responsible for this senseless act of violence,” Magistrado said. “We also call on anyone with information that may aid the investigation to immediately coordinate with the nearest police station. Together, we can ensure that those responsible are held fully accountable under the law.” Ometer said PRO-13 remains steadfast in its commitment to delivering swift, impartial, and thorough investigations while upholding the rule of law and ensuring the safety and security of every community in the Caraga region.

Senators slam TRO on P85 daily minimum wage hike implementation. Senators on Monday, August 3 criticized the issuance of a temporary restraining order issued by a Pasig City Regional Trial Court against the implementation of the P85 daily minimum wage increase in Metro Manila. The petition filed by Readycon Trading and Construction Corp. and R-11 Builders, Inc. before Pasig RTC Branch 152 sought to stop the Regional Tripartite Wages and Productivity Board—NCR and the National Wages and Productivity Commission (NWPC) from implementing the expected wage increase until August 13. Sen. Raffy Tulfo pointed out that the court’s action is unacceptable since Article 126 of the Labor Code clearly states that no court, tribunal or other authority may issue a preliminary injunction, permanent injunction, or TRO against any hearing, action or proceeding of the Regional Wage Boards. Tulfo argued that an appeal should have gone through the proper process and been filed with the appropriate agency, which in this case, should have been the NWPC. “The wage increase is already meager dspite the continuous rise in the prices of goods, and now even that has been denied to our struggling workers who simply want to make ends meet,” Tulfo said in a statement. It may be recalled that the additional P85 in the daily minimum wage was divided into two phases—the P60, which took effect on July 25, while the remaining P25 increase will be implemented starting January 1, 2027.Tulfo lamented that the court’s action was a major blow to the livelihoods of Filipino workers. “Suspending their wage increase is an even greater violation of theri rights, especially amid the continuing rise in the prices of basic goods. The lives and livelihoods of laborerrs should take precedence in this matter,” he said. “The court should no longer interfere in this issue, and it would be better for these companies—who show no appreciation for the contributions of their workers to their businesses—to pursue their appeal through the proper process,” the senator said. Tulfo said he will soon file a bill to amend the provisions of Article 126 of the Labor Code so that there would no longer be confusion in the implementation of the law regarding wage hikes. Sen. Risa Hontiveros also lamented the decision of the court, pointing out that there are already solutions on the table that can be implemented by the government at this point in time. “First, the P85 wage hike must be implemented. It’s already a modest increase, and it’s even being paid in installments. Groups such as the Financial Executives Institute of the Philippines have already agreed to it, and some employers are prepared to provide the wage increase. So workers should not lose this pay raise simply because it has been blocked in court,” Hontiveros said. She said the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) and the Office of the Solicitor General (OSG) should fight the case so it can be dismissed as possible, or so the suspension of the wage hike can be lifted. “I also urge our business community: let us go through the administrative processes for exemption. Let us respect the law and the tripartite system in which workers, employers, and the government all have a voice,” she appealed. “If this system is bypassed, the predictability and industrial peace that allow businesses to thrive will be put at risk,” she stressed. Hontiveros also said that alongside higher wages, the government should pursue the lowering of electricity costs. She pointed out the government cannot give workers a wage increase with one hand only to take it back through higher electricity bills with the other. “When it comes to the wage hike and reducing electricity charges, we have solutions, we have the means, and we can fix this,” she said. Sen. Joel Villanueva, chairman of the Senate Committee on Labor and Employment said that while he respects the court’s decision he is confused by the ruling. Villanueva also cited the inacceptability of the TRO, citing Article 126 of the Labor Code. “As head of the Senate labor panel, I’m also saddened by this development. This increase is badly needed by our workers. I’m also confused by that decision primarily because of Article 126 of the Labor Code,” he said. “I’m more than willing to be corrected, but that is also my understanding of the law," added Villanueva. Nevertheless, Villanueva said he hope and pray that the matter be soon resolved and any legal questions regarding the wage increase would be clarified.

150 Manila youth hired in short‑term government jobs. A total of 150 students and out-of-school youth in Manila secured short-term jobs under the government’s Special Program for Employment of Students (SPES). The beneficiaries signed contracts on Monday through the city’s Public Employment Service Office (PESO) for an 11-day work program, giving them extra income for daily and school expenses. Manila Mayor Francisco "Isko Moreno" Domagoso led the deployment. He said the program supports the city’s push to address basic needs such as jobs, education, housing, and healthcare. “Ang layunin natin… makapagbigay ng extra income, lalo na sa mga nag-aaral at out-of-school youth (Our goal is to provide extra income, especially for students and out-of-school youth),” he said. Vice Mayor Chi Atienza said the program expands opportunities for young Manileños. “Itong programang ito ay nagpapakita na tunay na may malasakit ang ating alkalde… importante na mabigyan ng oportunidad ang kabataan (This program shows the mayor truly cares… it is important to give opportunities to the youth),” she said. The city also cited plans to expand access to education, including a five-story building for the Pamantasan ng Lungsod ng Maynila College of Medicine that could accommodate up to 5,000 students. The SPES beneficiaries were deployed with support from the city’s youth sector, alongside officials from PESO, the Manila Youth Bureau, and the SK Federation.

Mark Villar pushes for tax exemption to strengthem MSMEs, spur job creation. Senator Mark Villar has filed a measure seeking to exempt micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) from the Minimum Corporate Income Tax (MCIT) saying it is imperative to provide them much-needed tax relief as they serve as the key driver of the Philippine economy. Villar, in filing Senate Bill No. 2362, said MSMEs have provided significant contribution to the country yet many of them stil grapple with rising production costs, persistent inflation and other economic pressures. These challenges, he said, are further aggravated when inflation climbed to 7.2 percent in April 2026 following the declaration of a national energy emergency, leaving many MSMEs struggling to sustain their operations. “Our MSMEs are the backbone of the Philippine economy. They provide livelihood to millions of Filipinios, fuel local industries, and keep our communities economically active,” Villar said. "By giving them meaningful tax relief, we allow them to reinvest in their businesses, create more jobs, and contribute even more to our country’s development,” he added. Under the bill, Villar proposes exempting qualified MSMEs, as defined under the Magna Carta for MSMEs, from the MICT by amending the relevant provisions of the National Internal Revenue Code (NIRC). The bill also aims to reduce the tax burden on small businesses, enabling them to retain more capital for expansion, innovation, and job generation while improving thier competitiveness and resilience in a challenging economic environment. Villar said he hopes passage of the measure into law would give MSMEs more power to expand their operations, improve productivity, and continue driving inclusive economic growth across the country. “When our small businesses succeed, more Filipinos benefit through new jobs, stronger local economies and increased opportunities for families,” he said. “This measure is about giving our entrepreneurs the support they need to grow and helping ensure that economic progress reaches every community,” he reiterated.

Las Piñas National High School suspends face-to-face classes after fatal campus stabbing. Face-to-face classes at Las Piñas National High School (LPNHS) have been suspended for five days after the fatal stabbing of a 13-year-old student inside the campus on July 31. Principal Ignacio Son announced the suspension for junior and senior high school students from Aug. 3 to 7, citing Department of Education (DepEd) Order No. 14, s. 2026, and the directive of Las Piñas City Mayor April Aguilar. The school will temporarily shift to alternative learning modalities to allow students, teachers, and personnel time for mental health and psychosocial interventions. During the suspension, students will continue lessons through printed modules, worksheets, and assignments distributed or sent via the school’s official online platforms, including Google Classroom and class group chats. Son said psychosocial processing and counseling sessions will be conducted for students, teachers, and non-teaching staff in coordination with guidance advocates, mental health professionals, and the city government. “The school remains committed to ensuring the safety, well-being, and emotional recovery of the entire school community during this difficult period,” the statement read. The administration will also review and strengthen campus security measures, including safety protocols, coordination with law enforcement, and additional preventive steps before classes resume. Aguilar directed city agencies to provide psychological support to those affected and ordered the Las Piñas City Police to heighten visibility in public schools while security measures are under review. Nearby Saint Rose of Lima School, Inc. likewise announced a temporary shift in its learning modality as a precaution. The suspension follows the fatal stabbing of a 13-year-old student by a 14-year-old classmate inside the LPNHS campus after an alleged argument. Police said the case is under investigation, and the child in conflict with the law has been placed under custody in line with the Juvenile Justice and Welfare Act.

Delay on benefits, bonuses for health workers being addressed, Palace says. Malacañang assured health workers under the Department of Health (DOH) that the issues concerning the delayed benefits and performance-based bonuses are being addressed by the Marcos administration. Although Palace Press Officer and Communications Undersecretary Claire Castro noted that the delays did not happen during the term of President Marcos, but the matter is now being addressed. "Okay, noong 2021, of course, hindi pa po ito sakop ni Pangulong Marcos Jr. Pero sa ngayon po, ito po ay inaayos po (Okay, in 2021, of course, this was not yet under President Marcos Jr.'s administration. But at present, this is being addressed)," Castro said in a Palace briefing on Monday, Aug. 3. According to Castro, there are only a few issues raised by the Commission on Audit (COA) while the DOH has already sent a letter to the Department of Budget and Management (DBM) seeking clarification on these matters. The issues being clarified, she added, involve the medical allowance, particularly the verification of disbursement methods—such as whether payments are made directly through HMO providers or through cash reimbursement—as well as eligibility coverage and the required supporting documents. "So, ito iyong mga issues na kinakailangang maresolba (These are the issues that still need to be resolved)," Castro said. "Pero sa mga kababayan po natin na kayo naman po talaga ay benepisyaryo, makakaasa po kayo at inaayos lamang po ang mga issues para liwanagin po ito sa DBM (To our fellow citizens who are the rightful beneficiaries, you can rest assured that you will receive your benefits. The government is simply resolving these issues and clarifying them with the DBM)," the Palace official added. In a statement, the Alliance of Health Workers said the President "failed to acknowledge the long-overdue unpaid benefits still owed to thousands of health workers," stressing that "he made no commitment to release the unpaid P7,000 Medical Allowance, the long-delayed Performance-Based Bonus (PBB) for eligible health workers for 2021, 2022, and 2024, and other pending benefits that health workers have repeatedly demanded."

ICTSI profit jumps 25% as global port expansion drives record revenue. Razon-led International Container Terminal Services Inc. (ICTSI) posted a 25 percent increase in first-half recurring net income, propelled by robust trade volumes across its global network and revenue contributions from newly acquired terminals in Africa and Asia. In a statement, ICTSI said net income excluding nonrecurring items rose to $604.69 million for the six months through June, compared with the same period a year earlier. On a reported basis, net income attributable to equity holders climbed 22 percent to $589.98 million, reflecting a nonrecurring charge tied to the divestment of Yantai International Container Terminal in China's Shandong Province. Diluted earnings per share gained 23 percent to $0.289. Gross revenues from port operations surged 27 percent to $1.92 billion from $1.51 billion in the prior-year period. The top-line performance was driven by higher container volumes, favorable cargo mix, tariff adjustments, and expanding ancillary port services. Favorable foreign-exchange translation gains from the appreciation of the Mexican peso, Australian dollar, and Brazilian real also bolstered revenue, offsetting headwinds from a weaker Philippine peso and lower throughput in Iraq. Handled container volume reached 8.12 million twenty-foot equivalent units, or TEUs, up 16 percent from 6.99 million TEUs a year earlier. The volume expansion was primarily fueled by the integration of two newly added operations: Durban Gateway Terminal in South Africa, which ICTSI began operating in January, and Batu Ampar Container Terminal in Indonesia, added in September. Organic growth remained modest as broader geopolitical strains weighed on specific regions. Excluding contributions from the newly added terminals and the deconsolidated Yantai facility, consolidated volume grew one percent. Throughput in the Europe, Middle East, and Africa region faced downward pressure due to ongoing geopolitical conflict in the Middle East, which dragged down container volumes at Basra Gateway Terminal in Iraq. “ICTSI delivered a strong first half, with double-digit growth in volumes, revenues and earnings supported by contributions from recently added terminals and stable performance across our existing portfolio,” ICTSI Chairman and President Enrique K. Razon Jr. sai. “Despite a more challenging operating backdrop in some markets during the period, our diversified footprint continued to provide resilience,” he added. Consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, or Ebitda, rose 24 percent to $1.23 billion from $990.54 million. However, the company's Ebitda margin contracted to 64 percent from 66 percent, reflecting the lower-margin integration phase of newly acquired assets. Excluding new and discontinued operations, the Ebitda margin expanded slightly to 66 percent, underscoring the operational efficiency of ICTSI’s established terminals. Cash operating expenses climbed 39 percent to $529.34 million, driven by the cost overhead of the Durban facility, revenue-linked ancillary costs, fuel price increases connected to Middle East instability, and government-mandated salary adjustments. Excluding new acquisitions and divested units, operating expenses rose 17 percent. For the second quarter alone, net income grew 21 percent to $296.41 million as revenue jumped 25 percent to $958.73 million. Consolidated volume for the three-month period through June rose 15 percent to 4.03 million TEUs. ICTSI spent $320.05 million on capital expenditures during the first six months and reiterated its full-year capex forecast of $740 million. Capital outlays are targeted for expansion projects at Contecon Manzanillo in Mexico, ongoing development at flagship Manila International Container Terminal and other Philippine facilities, terminal upgrades in Brazil and the Democratic Republic of Congo, and new expansion initiatives in Honduras, Australia, and Ecuador.

Share BlueSky Email Facebook Linkedin Twitter Whatsapp Save Print Related Tags Russia Ukraine In this episode of War & Peace , Olga is joined by Sabine Fischer, senior fellow at the German Institute for International and Security Affairs (SWP), to discuss her book “The Chauvinist Threat: Russia’s War and the West’s Response”. They unpack how chauvinist politics – defined as a combination of imperialism, sexism and autocracy – have shaped Russian society and politics under President Vladimir Putin and helped pave the way for Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. They examine how the war has accelerated chauvinism in Russia, including through pressure on women to have children, rising domestic violence and the repression of feminist and LGBTQI+ activism, while also raising the war’s complex effects on gender relations in Ukraine. They also consider how different outcomes to the war could shape Russia’s future and politics across Europe, what guardrails liberal democracies, including those in the process of re-arming, have against chauvinist shifts, and whether and how chauvinist politics might be reversed. ORIGI, MESSIAS, ADLI E 25 MILIONI PER MILINKOVIC-SAVIC. LOTITO NE CHIEDE 35!!!. Il Milan, dopo lo scioccante siluramento di Paolo Maldini, punta al grande colpo per il calciomercato estivo: Sergej Milinkovic-Savic della Lazio . Lo ha riferito ' SportMediaset '. Il Diavolo, dunque, ha intenzione di andare all'assalto del centrocampista serbo, classe 1995 , che gioca nella Capitale dal 2015 e che ora sembra arrivato al momento dei saluti. Nonostante il contratto di Milinkovic-Savic scadrà tra un anno, il 30 giugno 2024 , il Presidente della Lazio, Claudio Lotito , continua a valutarlo molto. Si parla di 35-40 milioni di euro, per un giocatore che, in fin dei conti, in questa stagione con le Aquile di Maurizio Sarri si è riconfermato come uno dei centrocampisti più forti e completi del panorama calcistico mondiale. Motivo per cui il Milan, pur di metterlo a disposizione di Stefano Pioli in questo calciomercato estivo, sarebbe pronto ad offrire alla Lazio 25 milioni più ben tre contropartite tecniche individuati in Junior Messias , Divock Origi e Yacine Adli. Le contropartite tecniche sarebbero di gradimento per Mister Sarri e si adatterebbero facilmente al suo gioco spettacolare: Adli può ricoprire diversi ruoli del centrocampo e sarebbe un sostituto ideale del capitano biancoazzurro; Messias , visto il flop di Romero e l'età avanzata di Pedro, sarebbe un'ottima alternativa di fascia visto i tanti impegni che aspettano la Lazio; Origi sarebbe una discreta opzione a Ciro Immobile, lasciando crescere con tranquillità il talentuoso Cancellieri. La palla passa a Lotito che attende un rialzo di offerta magari intorno ai 30 milioni e l'inserimento di tre contropartite tecniche di buon livello per concludere l'affare.

Per dare un’idea del modo in cui viene messo in pratica il regolamento, prendiamo in esame un caso simile: il famoso petardo in testa a Dida nel derby di Milano del 2004-2005. In quel caso le autorità capiscono che la situazione non può avere seguito e inoltre il brasiliano resta a terra. Per questo motivo, viene assegnato il 3-0 a tavolino ai rossoneri. In sostanza, il West Ham al momento rischia solo una pesante sanzione pecuniaria e la squalifica del campo nella prossima edizione dell’Europa League. Un caso simile, alla Fiorentina , è capitato nella stessa competizione contro il Sivasspor, in Turchia. Alessandro Bianco riceve un pugno in faccia da un invasore di campo della squadra di casa. Il calciatore rimedia la frattura del setto nasale. Per i turchi è arrivata una dura sanzione, più l’impossibilità di andare allo stadio per una giornata per i tifosi.

LAGIORNATA MONDIALE DELLE TARTARUGHE MARINE. Sono già una dozzina i nidi censiti dal network tartarughe marine del WWF in Sicilia (proprio in queste ore sono in corso le operazioni di verifica e messa in sicurezza degli ultimi), e uno in Calabria. Il Mediterraneo, sebbene rappresenti solo una piccola percentuale della superficie totale degli oceani, lo 0.82%, ospita una straordinaria varietà di vita marina. Con oltre 17.000 specie diverse, questa regione è un importante hotspot di biodiversità marina. E tra questa vasta varietà di specie, le tartarughe marine occupano un posto speciale. Nel Mediterraneo, tre specie di tartarughe marine hanno fatto di queste acque la loro casa: la tartaruga comune (Caretta caretta, l’unica che vi si riproduce), la tartaruga verde (Chelonia mydas) e la tartaruga liuto (Dermochelys coriacea). Le tartarughe marine trascorrono la maggior parte della loro vita in mare, ma, come altri rettili, respirano aria tramite i polmoni. La deposizione delle uova è l’unica fase vitale che avviene sulla terraferma, di solito tra maggio e agosto nel Mediterraneo. Dopo l’accoppiamento, le femmine raggiungono la spiaggia per deporre le uova, che vengono incubate dal calore del sole (e del suolo) per circa due mesi. La temperatura influisce anche sul sesso delle tartarughe neonate: temperature superiori a 29°C tendono a produrre femmine, mentre temperature inferiori generano maschi. Dopo la deposizione delle uova, le femmine ritornano alle loro zone di alimentazione, che possono trovarsi anche a migliaia di chilometri di distanza dalle zone di riproduzione. Una volta raggiunta la maturità sessuale, intorno ai 20-30 anni, le tartarughe ritornano alle stesse aree di riproduzione per deporre le uova. La loro capacità di orientarsi durante queste lunghe migrazioni è influenzata dall’incredibile abilità di percepire il campo geomagnetico terrestre, una sorta di sesto senso di queste antichissime specie. L’impatto dei cambiamenti climatici. L’aumento delle temperature globali influisce direttamente sull’habitat di queste creature e sulle risorse di cui dipendono per la loro sopravvivenza, oltre che sulle correnti. Uno degli effetti più evidenti è l’aumento della temperatura dell’acqua. Le tartarughe marine sono specie ectotermiche, il che significa che la loro temperatura corporea dipende dall’ambiente circostante. Con l’aumento delle temperature marine, le tartarughe possono trovarsi in situazioni di stress termico, poiché non sono in grado di regolare la propria temperatura interna. Questo può influire sul loro metabolismo, sulla loro capacità di digerire il cibo e sull’efficienza riproduttiva.

BONUS VACANZE: SCADENZA DELLE DOMANDE IL 30 GIUGNO. La procedura per la richiesta del Bonus vacanze va effettuata solamente online tramite la app “Io” da smartphone. Basta munirsi di Spid o della carta d’identità elettronica. Lo possono richiedere soltanto i nuclei familiari con un reddito Isee sotto i 40.000 euro e può essere speso solo per un soggiorno in Italia entro la fine dell’anno. Una volta ottenuto il Bonus, la prenotazione della vacanza non può essere effettuata su siti online: quindi non è possibile prenotare né con Booking né con Airbnb o con altri siti di prenotazione. Bisogna, invece, prenotare tramite agenzie viaggi o o tour operator tradizionali o direttamente con la struttura scelta nella meta di villeggiatura. Ecco gli step per fare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze: se non si è già scaricata la app “Io” in passato sul proprio smartphone è possibile farlo sia per telefoni Apple sia per Android; la prima volta che si scarica la app viene richiesta la registrazione che è possibile fare più facilmente digitando un Pin a scelta o, per chi è più pratico, attraverso il riconoscimento biometrico (impronta digitale o riconoscimento del volto); una volta entrati nella app, bisogna selezionare la sezione “pagamenti” e quindi il Bonus vacanze; a questo punto è necessario inserire le informazioni richieste, tra cui il valore dell’Isee; se tutte le informazioni inserite sono corrette, la app genera un codice associato al vostro Bonus vacanze con un QrCode; sia il codice sia il QrCode devono essere mostrati alla struttura al momento del pagamento. N.B. Prima di effettuare la richiesta del Bonus vacanze è bene tenere sotto mano sia la propria identità Spid sia la carta d’identità elettronica e i dati del proprio Isee (chi non lo ricorda può recuperarlo all’Inps o al proprio Caf). Il Bonus di un valore massimo di 500 euro è rivolto alle famiglie italiane composte da almeno tre persone. Per i nuclei familiari composti da due persone il Bonus vacanze scende a 300 euro, ma lo possono ottenere anche i single, in questo caso il valore è di 150 euro.
